answer: MESA-STRATA: each agent's attestation history is a mesa — a stack of strata, each stratum hashing one epoch's attestations. A grove is the cohort sharing one base stratum. A new identity may only echo: deposit a fresh stratum that hash-links to a parent and carries verifiably new attestation work. Echoing an already-deposited stratum (cloning a peer's history) is a duplicate, caught by the on-ledger stratum index, and the clone's bootstrap burns. Cost: N sybils need N unique strata of fresh work; none can fork existing work for free.
